fieldValues.title: Advisory diagnostics, as a convention first
fieldValues.decision_question: How should repo validate tell advice apart from real problems?
fieldValues.context: Relayed from the owner's working session on 2026-10-10 (the owner was away from a computer); awaiting the owner's ratification. Advice-only (SHOULD-level) checks are reported as warnings, so warning counts stop meaning anything: the spec repo once showed 46 warnings with about one real; srs-programme shows 22 harmless ones on every run.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A: a real advisory severity (contract change, RFC). B: group the summary only. C: leave it. Chosen: A, introduced as a convention.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Introduce an advisory level below warning, first as a convention: advice-only checks are marked advisory in an additive way and counted separately, with no breaking change. It becomes a standard only after review.
fieldValues.rationale: Too much information is the same as noise; we want the signal. A warning must mean act on this.
fieldValues.revisit_when: After at least four weeks in use across the repos that validate in CI (srs, srs-programme, muDemocracy.org): are warnings acted on and advisories still read? If yes, standardise via an RFC; if not, withdraw.
fieldValues.next_steps: WG Third-party ready builds the simple version: https://github.com/the-greenman/srs-rust/issues/700
